- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative or mixed (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak if sentiment peaks recently.
- If true price rises >5% from recent 7-day average, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- Model underestimates when sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period; add 0.3–0.8% buffer to forecast if sentiment drops.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 oscillations, model often misjudges mean reversion; apply slight downward bias (0.5–1.0%) to forecast.
